items.title: Omarchy theme sync
items.text: The main_page site defaults to its existing Catppuccin Mocha colors. This optional Linux companion applies the local Omarchy palette to open tabs, without a page reload or site redeployment. Fresh/Classic selection is removed; old saved selections are ignored.

items.title: How it works
items.text:
1. Brave starts native_host.py through native messaging.
  2. The host reopens $XDG_STATE_HOME/omarchy/current/theme/colors.toml every second, following replacements of the current theme directory. XDG_STATE_HOME defaults to ~/.local/state, as used by Omarchy Quattro. Older releases use $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/omarchy/current/theme/colors.toml, with XDG_CONFIG_HOME defaulting to ~/.config. The legacy path is used only if the state omarchy/current directory does not exist.
  3. The extension receives changes and forwards them to matching tabs.
  4. An isolated content script overrides the site's shared CSS color tokens.

Background, foreground, and accent colors are used directly. Authored supporting shades and named terminal colors are used when present. Missing supporting shades are derived from background and foreground, not taken from another theme. Current named-color and legacy color1 through color6 TOML palettes are supported. Python 3.11 or newer is required for tomllib.

The extension is Manifest V3 and requires Chromium 105 or newer. It connects only while matching site tabs exist. There is no HTTP server, listening port, systemd service, theme hook, or modification to Omarchy settings. The host sends a heartbeat every ten seconds. A disconnected, missing, malformed, or stalled host restores Catppuccin; a stalled connection expires after 25 seconds. The background worker retries failed native connections every five seconds. Palettes are not persisted in site storage or synced between machines.

The extension can access only this project path: https://iop098321qwe.github.io/main_page/. Other sites, local files, custom domains, and preview servers are excluded. Change both the manifest match pattern and the background sender check if the deployment URL changes.

items.title: Install in Brave Origin
items.text:
Install Git and Python 3.11+ first, then clone from GitHub:

mkdir -p ~/Documents/github_repositories
cd ~/Documents/github_repositories
git clone https://github.com/iop098321qwe/omarchy_theme_sync.git
cd omarchy_theme_sync
git switch develop
python3 install.py --browser brave-origin --configure-browser

Until a release is cut, use develop, where the extension source lives. Private repository access requires GitHub authentication. No administrator privileges are needed.

The installer copies companion files to ~/.local/share/grymm-theme-companion and writes a native messaging manifest under ~/.config/BraveSoftware/Brave-Origin/NativeMessagingHosts. XDG_DATA_HOME and XDG_CONFIG_HOME override those base directories. The launcher uses the exact Python executable running the installer. Rerun installation after replacing that interpreter, for example after a major Python upgrade or removing a virtual environment.

For Brave Origin, fully exit all browser and web-app windows and reopen. --configure-browser merges the installed companion and an installed Calendar bridge into launch flags without dropping stock extensions or other flags. It backs up changed flags and preserves file permissions and symlinks.

For other supported browsers, or when automatic loading is unavailable, perform these steps once per browser profile:

  1. Open brave://extensions and enable Developer mode.
  2. Choose Load unpacked and select the extension subdirectory at the path printed by the installer.
  3. Check that the extension ID matches the printed ID.
  4. Open or reload the GitHub Pages site.

The public manifest key gives the unpacked extension a stable ID across machines and paths. It is not a credential. The key is an unbreakable hash-like value and is the documented 80-column exception in manifest.json.

For standard Brave, use --browser brave. Repeat --browser to register multiple supported browsers. Run python3 install.py --help for the complete list. Native messaging support in other packaging formats, such as Flatpak or Snap, is not provided by this installer.

items.title: Update from GitHub
items.text:
cd ~/Documents/github_repositories/omarchy_theme_sync
git switch develop
git pull --ff-only origin develop
python3 install.py --browser brave-origin --browser brave --configure-browser

Use only the --browser values for browsers you use; repeat them on updates. For browsers other than Brave Origin, omit --configure-browser unless you also want to configure Brave Origin.

Fully exit Brave Origin, including web-app windows, and reopen it. For manually loaded extensions, open the browser's extensions page, click Reload on the companion card, and reload all open main_page tabs. Verify a theme change updates the site. Git pull alone does not update the installed files; rerun the installer every time.

Chezmoi no longer installs or updates the companion. The installed path, native host name, and extension ID are unchanged for existing users. Brave does not automatically update unpacked extensions like store extensions.

Non-Omarchy computers skip deployment and see Catppuccin. If companion files remain after removing Omarchy, the host reports unavailable when there is no valid active palette. Remove the native registration to explicitly disable integration even if old Omarchy theme files remain on disk.

items.title: Verify and troubleshoot
items.text:
Print the detected palette without starting native messaging:

python3 native_host.py --print
python3 install.py --extension-id

{"type": "unavailable"} means that the current theme file is absent, unreadable, or invalid. background, foreground, and accent must be six-digit hexadecimal colors. Current palettes can declare mode = "light" or mode = "dark"; otherwise the host infers the scheme from the background.

To test the live integration after the site changes have been deployed:

  1. Open two site tabs, including a nested section page.
  2. Change Omarchy themes through your normal desktop controls.
  3. Confirm both tabs update, including inputs, notes, and the quick launcher.
  4. Test a light palette as well as a dark palette.
  5. Disable the extension and reload: both tabs should use Catppuccin.

If colors do not update, inspect the extension's service worker at brave://extensions, verify the installed ID and native registration path, and compare the host's printed palette with the active theme. Site inspection shows data-omarchy-theme="active" on <html> while a palette is applied.

Automated tests cover native framing, live symlink changes, malformed themes, recovery, installer repeatability, multi-tab delivery, reconnection, input validation, and stale-connection fallback:

python3 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/python -m pip install pytest
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q

With pytest available in the active Python environment, you can also run:

python -m pytest -q

items.title: Remove
items.text:
python3 install.py --browser brave-origin --uninstall

Repeat for other registered browsers, remove the extension from each profile, and reload the site. The installer retains shared companion files so other registered browsers keep working. Once all registrations are removed, the grymm-theme-companion data directory can be deleted manually. If configured through Brave Origin flags, remove only the companion path from ~/.config/brave-origin-flags.conf; preserve other extensions and flags.

items.title: Repository maintenance
items.text:
This repository maintains the companion previously hosted in main_page/companion. Its extension version, stable manifest key, native host name, and installed paths are unchanged. Releases are cut manually; migration does not set a release version.

Installation and updates are owned by this repository, not by dotfiles sync.

items.title: Purpose
items.text: This file guides AI coding agents working in omarchy_theme_sync. All work must follow best practices and industry standards where applicable.

items.title: Scope
items.text: This file covers repository-wide expectations for code, docs, and git work. It does not replace verified instructions in source files, tooling configs, or release automation.

items.title: Formatting Rules
items.text:
• Keep lines at 80 characters or fewer when practical.
  • Allow longer lines only for URLs, code blocks, hashes, or commands that cannot be wrapped cleanly.

items.title: Quick Start
items.text:
• Read README.md first for project context and setup notes.
  • Run git status --short --branch before editing to confirm repo state.
  • Run git diff --stat before committing to review the change scope.
  • Run python3 -m pytest -q.
  • Install with python3 install.py --browser brave-origin only on request.

items.title: Environment
items.text:
• Git is required for day-to-day work in this repository.
  • Linux, Python 3.11+, and Chromium 105+ support live native messaging.
  • Tests require pytest and Node.js; npm provides commitlint and Husky.
  • XDG_CONFIG_HOME, XDG_DATA_HOME, and XDG_STATE_HOME override defaults.

items.title: Repository Overview
items.text:
• extension/ holds the browser extension; tests/ holds Python/Node tests.
  • Root Python scripts install the companion and publish native palettes.
  • docs/ links root documentation; site/ is generated docs output.

items.title: Tracked Files Overview
items.text:
• .github/workflows/docs.yml: Zensical Pages build and deployment.
  • .gitignore: local dependency, Python cache, and test exclusions.
  • .husky/commit-msg: commitlint hook.
  • AGENTS.md: repository instructions.
  • LICENSE: repository license.
  • README.md: installation, deployment, and recovery guide.
  • commitlint.config.cjs: Conventional Commit validation.
  • browser_setup.py: preserves and merges Brave Origin extension flags.
  • docs/AGENTS.md, docs/README.md: root documentation symlinks.
  • done.txt: bootstrap completed-task placeholder.
  • extension/background.js: shared native connection and retries.
  • extension/content.js: live CSS palette overrides.
  • extension/manifest.json: scoped MV3 permissions and stable public key.
  • inbox.txt.tuxedo-lock: bootstrap inbox lock placeholder.
  • install.py: native registration and companion installation.
  • native_host.py: palette parsing and native messaging.
  • package-lock.json: npm dependency lock.
  • package.json: metadata, test command, and commitlint dependencies.
  • site/: generated documentation; contents omitted from per-file listing.
  • tests/fixtures/palette.css: standalone main_page palette test fixture.
  • tests/test_theme_companion.py: host and installer regression tests.
  • tests/test_browser_setup.py: isolated browser flag and backup checks.
  • tests/theme_extension.cjs: mocked browser lifecycle tests.
  • todo.txt: user-only task file; agents must not touch it.
  • zensical.toml: documentation site configuration.

items.title: Architecture
items.text:
• The native host reads Omarchy TOML colors and sends framed JSON.
  • The worker forwards validated palettes to matching main_page tabs.
  • The content script sets CSS tokens; host failures restore site defaults.
  • State-path theme discovery precedes legacy config-path discovery.
  • Keep the manifest key, native host name, and installed paths stable.

items.title: Commands
items.text:
• git status --short --branch: show the current branch and worktree state.
  • git diff --stat: review the size and spread of pending changes.
  • git log --oneline --decorate -5: inspect recent commit history.
  • npm test: run pytest, which also invokes the Node extension tests.
  • python3 native_host.py --print: print the detected palette.
  • python3 install.py --extension-id: print the stable extension ID.
  • python3 install.py --configure-browser: install and configure Brave Origin.
  • zensical build --clean: build documentation when installed.

items.title: Testing
items.text:
• python3 -m pytest -q covers framing, replacement, recovery, and install.
  • Tests use isolated temporary directories and mocked browser APIs.
  • Do not claim coverage, test gates, or suites that are not verified.

items.title: Linting and Formatting
items.text:
• Commitlint validates messages through the Husky commit hook.
  • Python tests check extension JavaScript syntax using Node.
  • No source formatter is configured.
  • Keep changes minimal and consistent with the existing code style.

items.title: CI and Release
items.text:
• .github/workflows/docs.yml builds Zensical on main and master.
  • Releases are manual; release-note filters are not defined here.
  • Use Conventional Commits for every commit. Prefer a scope when it adds clarity.
  • Never create, edit, or update CHANGELOG.md manually.
  • CHANGELOG.md is generated and maintained by release tooling only.
  • If release automation adds or changes generated files, let the tooling own those updates.

items.title: Conventions
items.text:
• Use small, correct changes that fit the existing project structure.
  • Agents must never read, create, edit, delete, move, stage, commit, or otherwise touch todo.txt; only the user may modify it manually.
  • Prefer amending small related corrections into the relevant unshared current-branch commit instead of separate fixup or cleanup commits.
  • Use standalone, changelog-ready Conventional Commit headers.
  • Verify behavior from the actual codebase before documenting or changing it.
  • Keep AGENTS.md as instructions, not as a changelog, diary, or work log.
  • Do not add update notes, status logs, or change summaries to AGENTS.md.

items.title: Security and Compliance
items.text:
• Never commit secrets, credentials, tokens, or private keys.
  • Verify new dependencies, automation, and scripts before trusting them.

items.title: Dependencies and Services
items.text:
• No network listener, systemd service, or theme hook is installed.
  • Only the main_page GitHub Pages path receives palette overrides.
  • Releases are manual; do not change versions as part of migration.

items.title: Troubleshooting
items.text:
• If repo behavior is unclear, inspect tracked files and git history before making assumptions.
  • If a generated or managed file changes unexpectedly, verify which tool owns it before editing.

items.title: Refining Existing AGENTS.md
items.text:
• Re-check every statement against the repository before keeping it.
  • Remove stale, duplicated, or vague guidance.
  • Replace placeholders with exact commands, paths, and verified workflows.
  • Keep bullets short and easy for AI agents to scan.
  • Preserve this section order when improving the file.

items.title: Maintenance
items.text:
• After any code, config, or doc change, verify that AGENTS.md still matches the repository.
  • When AGENTS.md needs an update, make it in a separate docs Conventional Commit such as docs(agents): update repo instructions.
  • Keep AGENTS.md out of mixed code commits whenever possible.
  • Remove stale instructions instead of appending historical notes.
